title: Ordered affine chart equation for diagonal section pasting
statement:
Fix the finite coefficient stage $\Lambda=A_{E,n}$, $n\geq1$, of [def-pur-conventions], with the specified global field $k=\overline{\mathbf F}_q$, $\ell\ne\operatorname{char}(k)$ and finite extension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$. Let $f:X\to Y$ and $g:Y\to Z$ be smooth separated finite-type morphisms of pure relative dimensions $d,e\geq0$ between finite-type $k$-schemes [def-weil-finite-type-morphism, def-weil-proper-morphism, def-sbc-smooth-morphisms]. Use the small pro-etale constructible exceptional inverse images and derived operations of [def-weil-exceptional-inverse-image, def-weil-derived-pullback-tensor-hom]. Put $\omega_h=Rh^!\Lambda$ and let $c_{v,u}:R(vu)^!\xrightarrow{\sim}Ru^!Rv^!$ be the conjugate of compact-support composition [thm-sf-comp-composition, def-weil-pbc-composite-adjunction, def-weil-pbc-adjunction-conjugate]. Let $\theta_{h,M}:Lh^*M\otimes^L\omega_h\to Rh^!M$ be the specified tensor map [def-pur-co-smoothness]. For composable smooth maps $u,v$ define
$$\sigma_{u,v}=c_{v,u,\Lambda}^{-1}\circ\theta_{u,\omega_v}\circ\mathrm{sym}:\omega_u\otimes^LLu^*\omega_v\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_{vu}.$$
For $h=f,g,gf$, write $W_h=\operatorname{dom}(h)\times_{\operatorname{cod}(h)}\operatorname{dom}(h)$, $p_h$ for its first projection, $\Delta_h$ for the diagonal, $C_h=L\Delta_h^*\omega_{p_h}$ [def-pur-section-invariant], and $\alpha_h:C_h\xrightarrow{\sim}\omega_h$ for the specified diagonal base-change map [lem-pur-diagonal-base-change].

Put $Q=X\times_ZY$, $W=X\times_ZX$, $a:W\to Q$, $(x_1,x_2)\mapsto(x_1,f(x_2))$, $b:Q\to X$, $(x,y)\mapsto x$, $t=\Delta_{gf}:X\to W$, and $s=(\operatorname{id}_X,f):X\to Q$. These formulas denote the maps induced by the fibre-product universal property [def-pc-fibre-product]. Then $at=s$, $ba=p_{gf}$, and the Cartesian base-change maps identify $C_f\cong Lt^*\omega_a$ and $Lf^*C_g\cong Ls^*\omega_b$. Define the section-pasting comparison, using these maps and the monoidal pullback reassociation, by
$$\kappa:C_f\otimes^LLf^*C_g\xrightarrow{\sim}Lt^*(\omega_a\otimes^LLa^*\omega_b)\xrightarrow{Lt^*\sigma_{a,b}}C_{gf}.$$
 For a separated finite-type $k$-scheme $B$, put $P_r=\mathbf A^r_B\to B$ [def-sbc-affine-space], let $z_r:B\to\mathbf A^r_B$ be its zero section, and put $D_r=Lz_r^*\omega_{P_r}$. Let $q:\mathbf A^{d+e}_B=\mathbf A^d_{\mathbf A^e_B}\to\mathbf A^e_B$. Base change for the square defining $q$ identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*\omega_q$ with $D_d$, while pullback composition identifies $Lz_{d+e}^*Lq^*\omega_{P_e}$ with $D_e$. Define
$$\nu_{d,e}:D_d\otimes^LD_e\xrightarrow{\sim}Lz_{d+e}^*(\omega_q\otimes^LLq^*\omega_{P_e})\xrightarrow{Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}}D_{d+e}.$$
For the present affine schemes X,Y,Z and specified compatible etale [def-weil-etale-morphism] coordinate charts $U\to\mathbf A^d_V$, $V\to\mathbf A^e_T$ for $f,g$, with $U=X,V=Y,T=Z$ (no open-restriction assertion is included), the coordinate differences in the second factors of the diagonal pairs identify $C_f|_U$, $Lf^*C_g|_U$, $C_{gf}|_U$ with $D_d,D_e,D_{d+e}$ over $B=U$. Under these comparisons, $\kappa|_U=\nu_{d,e}$. These are the canonical etale exceptional-pullback comparisons and monoidal pullback comparisons, and use no diagonal orientation or Tate-twist identification. Use the canonical normalization of the constructed comparisons from [def-pur-diagonal-section-pasting-data].

proof.text: On the compatible affine charts, [lem-pur-affine-difference-tower-factorization] supplies the actual Cartesian square defining $R$ and the etale maps $G,H,J,F$, with $Gs=z_e$ and $Ft=z_{d+e}$. The Cartesian square $q=P_d\times_BP_e$ and the canonical monoidal pullback comparison give the two inputs $D_d,D_e$ of $\nu_{d,e}$, whose remaining arrow is $Lz_{d+e}^*\sigma_{q,P_e}$. Apply [lem-pur-etale-cartesian-tower-tensor-comparison] with $p=P_e$; pull its final identity along $t$, identifying $Lt^*LF^*=Lz_{d+e}^*$ and $Lt^*La^*LG^*=Lz_e^*$ by derived pullback composition [lem-weil-pbc-proetale-derived-pullback-composition], and precompose with $\gamma_f\otimes\gamma_g$. By [lem-pur-difference-coordinate-section-identifications] its two input maps are precisely $\chi_f,\chi_g$ and its output map is $\chi_{gf}$. Thus the identity reads $\chi_{gf}\kappa=\nu_{d,e}(\chi_f\otimes\chi_g)$, as required. Empty charts and zero blocks are included in those lemmas; no orientation has entered.

lean.statement:
theorem diagonalSectionPastingChart (P : PurityFiniteSetting.{u}) {X Y Z : Scheme.{u}}
    (d e : ℕ) (f : X ⟶ Y) (g : Y ⟶ Z)
    [IsAffine X] [IsAffine Y] [IsAffine Z]
    [IsNoetherian X] [IsNoetherian Y] [IsNoetherian Z]
    [IsSeparated f] [LocallyOfFiniteType f] [QuasiCompact f]
    [IsSeparated g] [LocallyOfFiniteType g] [QuasiCompact g]
    [SmoothOfRelativeDimension d f] [SmoothOfRelativeDimension e g]
    (aZ : Z ⟶ Spec (.of P.field.k)) [LocallyOfFiniteType aZ] [QuasiCompact aZ]
    (x : X ⟶ A d Y) (y : Y ⟶ A e Z) [Etale x] [Etale y]
    (hx : x ≫ pr d Y = f) (hy : y ≫ pr e Z = g) :
    letI := P.comparedExponent (𝟙 (Spec (.of P.field.k)))
    ChartEquation P.Coefficient P d e f g aZ x y hx hy
